item.title: Arch Manning, Longhorns avoid scare against Texas A&M to punch ticket to SEC Championship Game
item.description: Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns survived a turnover-filled rivalry battle with Texas A&M, with Tawfiq Byard's pick highlighting a tense night.
item.content:encoded:
Texas came into Friday's game against Texas A&M in good shape. They were on track to take on Georgia in the SEC Championship game and also earn a spot in the College Football Playoff.

Of course, that all hinged on them taking care of the Aggies.

In the first quarter, Texas A&M stood tall defensively to hold the Longhorns to just a field goal. Unfortunately, the Aggies also dealt with some sloppiness on special teams and failed to put any points on the board during a promising-looking drive late in the frame.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

It didn't take too much longer for Arch Manning and the Texas offense to find the end zone. Manning found wide receiver Cam Coleman for six with a short, three-yard touchdown pass.

The Aggies got rid of their goose egg with a late first-half field goal to send this game to the room with the Longhorns leading 10-3.

That is a result you've got to think the Aggies would be pleased with, even if there were some elements of their game to clean up.

As the second half got underway, the Aggies forced the Longhorns to punt on their first possession, but then came another miscue.

Texas A&M receiver Mario Craver caught a pass for ten yards, but fumbled the ball, which was recovered by the Longhorns.

The play was reviewed and upheld after it was confirmed that Craver had made the catch before fumbling.

That gave Texas a short field, but the Aggies' defense managed to stand pat and held them to a field goal that made it a two-possession game.

Texas A&M responded with a field goal of their own, then their defense made a massive stop to force a turnover on downs. Unfortunately for them, the offense couldn't capitalize as the Longhorns held them to a three-and-out.

But once again, the Aggies' defense became the story as Tawfiq Byard picked off Arch Manning on the goal line.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Yet the A&M offense couldn’t capitalize, turning the ball over on downs around midfield.

Texas tacked on a field goal, which once again made it a two-score game with just 5:19 left, and that was all they needed. Texas took the victory by a score of 16-6.

Surely, they'll take the win... but they probably weren't ready to sweat for it that much.

Manning finished the night completing 18 of 34 passing attempts for 143 yards, a touchdown, and one pick.

The win locks in a Georgia-Texas SEC Championship Game, and should also punch the Longhorns a ticket to the College Football Playoff.

item.title: Former SEC head coach who landed in the Group of 5 abruptly steps down after underwhelming five-year run
item.description: Joe Moorhead is out at Akron football after five seasons, ending a run that saw the Zips go 2-10 this year and never post a winning record under his watch.
item.content:encoded:
Joe Moorhead exited Mississippi State in 2019 after a two-year stint as head coach in the Southeastern Conference. He was then named Oregon's offensive coordinator.

Two years later, Moorhead returned to the head-coaching ranks, taking on the challenge of turning around a program competing at the Group of 5 level.

After compiling a 15-44 record over five seasons at Akron, Moorhead says he is ready for another challenge.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Moorhead released a statement saying he decided to step down to pursue other opportunities.

"After careful consideration and thoughtful discussions with my family, I informed University of Akron officials of my decision to pursue other opportunities at the conclusion of this season," he wrote on social media after the Zips' 17-9 loss to Buffalo on Friday.

"I am thankful to the school administrators, past and present, for providing me with the chance to lead this team for the past five seasons."

"Lastly, I would like to express my most sincere gratitude to everyone who poured their heart and soul into this program, especially and most importantly our players. My family and I are excited for the next chapter in our journey and wish Zips football nothing but the best moving forward."

The Zips finished the 2026 season with a 2-10 record. None of Moorhead’s five seasons at Akron ended with a winning record, with the 2025 season's 5-7 mark representing the best finish of his tenure.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL COACHING CAROUSEL COULD EXPLODE AS LINCOLN RILEY AND DEION SANDERS FACE MOUNTING PRESSURE

Moorhead held various assistant coaching positions at Akron from 2004 to 2008. He later landed his first head coaching job at his alma mater, Fordham, in 2012. Moorhead is credited for guiding Fordham to three consecutive FCS playoff appearances.

He went 38-13 and led the Rams to the FCS playoffs in each of his final three seasons. Moorhead's resume also includes a two-year stint as Penn State’s offensive coordinator. He was fired by Mississippi State after posting a 14-12 record over two seasons, capped by a win over in-state rival Ole Miss in the Egg Bowl.

There are now 11 head-coaching vacancies at the FBS level following Moorhead’s departure.

One FBS school has already filled its vacancy, with Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann agreeing to a five-year contract to become Florida State’s next head coach. Schumann is expected to remain in his current role through next week’s SEC Championship Game and potentially into the College Football Playoff.

item.title: Former Bears star Revie Sorey, who blocked for Walter Payton, dead at 73
item.description: Former Chicago Bears guard Revie Sorey, who blocked for Walter Payton and later championed disadvantaged youth, has died at 73, a friend said.
item.content:encoded:
Former Chicago Bears offensive lineman Revie Sorey, who blocked for the legendary Walter Payton, died Thursday at 73.

Sorey died at Northwestern Memorial Hospital, Anita Efron, a Chicago attorney and one of Sorey's closest friends, said, according to the Chicago Sun-Times.

The Bears drafted Sorey in the fifth round of the 1975 NFL Draft out of Illinois, and he spent his entire nine-year career in Chicago. He played guard for all 109 games (77 starts) of his career.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Following his retirement from football, the Brooklyn, New York, native dedicated his post-playing life to helping disadvantaged youth in Chicago. He served as director of educational services at Ada S. McKinley Community Services.

With Efron, Sorey also founded the Revie Sorey Trunk Scholarship Program, which helped first-generation college-bound Chicago students go to school prepared, as they would get everything from computers to bedding.

"Everybody talks about his great infectious smile and how everybody he met became his buddy, his friend and how he went out of his way to make people feel special and guide people through their lives," Efron said, according to the Chicago Sun-Times.

"I am getting literally hundreds of texts and emails from people who Revie helped. He just wanted to uplift people and show them how they could soar and be their best self," Efron told the outlet. "Everybody has said that there’s a connection with the Bears getting that win on Thanksgiving, the day he died, and, yeah, I think so, too."

Sorey's wife, Suzy O’Malley-Sorey, died of pancreatic cancer in 2011.

Sorey suffered a stroke in March 2012 that left him unable to speak or walk, and he required around-the-clock care following the health incident. He eventually regained limited use of his speech after therapy.

In 2016, Sorey's son, Trace Sorey, died in an accidental drowning in a Los Angeles pool at 24 years old.

item.title: LA Olympics partnership with oil company prompts climate activist outrage, as board member resigns in protest
item.description: Rita Kampalath resigned from a Los Angeles Olympic environmental advisory group over the LA28 Phillips 66 sponsorship deal, citing fossil fuel concerns.
item.content:encoded:
An American oil company has signed on to help bring the 2028 Olympics to Los Angeles, potentially reducing the financial risk for California taxpayers. But the partnership has prompted backlash from climate activists and local politicians, and now a Los Angeles County official has resigned from an Olympic advisory group in protest.

Los Angeles County Chief Sustainability Officer Rita Kampalath announced Tuesday she was resigning from an Olympic environmental advisory group over a sponsorship deal between the organizers of the 2028 Games and the oil company Phillips 66.

The Texas-based oil company reached an agreement earlier this month to become the official fuel partner of the Olympics, Paralympics and Team USA.

LAPD CHIEF WARNS LOS ANGELES NOT PREPARED TO SECURE 2028 OLYMPICS DUE TO STAFFING SHORTAGES

The company will help fuel thousands of vehicles and equipment needed to put on the Games. It will also help support an Olympic torch relay that will take the flame through all 50 states.

Now some liberal officials in California, including Kampalath, are pushing back.

"The Games should represent the future Los Angeles is working to build, not the fossil fuel dependence we are working so hard to leave behind," Kampalath wrote in a LinkedIn post announcing her decision.

Kampalath is not leaving her county government job. She is stepping away from a group tasked with advising an Olympic-related fund that supports environmental projects, including wildfire prevention and ocean protection. She also clarified that her decision was personal and did not represent the county's position.

Other Los Angeles City Council members have also spoken out against the partnership.

Councilmember Hugo Soto-Martínez called the deal "disgusting," while Councilmember Katy Yaroslavsky called on Olympic organizers to drop the sponsorship, according to LAist.

LA HOTEL LEADERS WARN MAYOR BASS' $30 WAGE MANDATE IS KILLING BUSINESS AHEAD OF WORLD CUP, OLYMPICS

But another member of the council warned that doing so could come at a cost to the people they represent.

"Turning down this sponsorship would put more financial risk on Los Angeles taxpayers," Councilmember Tim McOsker told LAist.

Environmental activists are now circulating a petition calling on Olympic organizers to end their relationship with the company.

However, organizers have given no indication that they intend to back out of the deal.

LA28, the organization responsible for putting on the Games, has said its environmental commitments remain unchanged. Those commitments include using renewable electricity at competition venues, encouraging spectators to use public transportation and avoiding the construction of new permanent Olympic facilities.

Meanwhile, the Phillips 66 partnership will extend beyond Los Angeles. The company will also provide fuel to the U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Training Center in Colorado Springs and sponsor the 2028 U.S. Olympic and Paralympic track and field trials.

More than 15,000 athletes from around the world are expected to participate in the Olympics and Paralympics in 2028, when Los Angeles will host the Summer Olympics for the first time since 1984.

Los Angeles is preparing to host its third Olympics, and putting on the Games won't be cheap.

The estimated cost of hosting the event has grown to more than $7 billion, according to a January report from the city's administrative officer.

Olympic organizers rely heavily on corporate sponsorships and ticket sales to pay for the Games. But the city of Los Angeles has agreed to cover potential financial shortfalls, meaning taxpayers could ultimately be responsible if organizers don't bring in enough money.

item.title: Zeldin touts 'best-case scenario' after massive controlled detonation in Iowa
item.description: EPA chief Lee Zeldin says air monitoring after an Iowa Army Ammunition Plant detonation found zero detectable airborne lead, calling it a best-case scenario.
item.content:encoded:
Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin described initial air monitoring results after Wednesday's controlled detonation of a hazardous chemical stockpile in Iowa as a "best-case scenario" as officials prepare to release the results of additional environmental testing.

Speaking in an interview on Fox News Friday, Zeldin said four air monitoring stations positioned downwind of the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant recorded no detectable airborne lead after the controlled detonation.

"We only have measurements of 0.0, sometimes referred to as zero detect, sometimes referred to as non detect," Zeldin said.

"It's not that we just had a small elevation of lead being detected in our air monitoring," Zeldin added. "We had 0.0 readings on our air monitoring, and that's certainly a best-case scenario."

US ARMY TO PROCEED WITH IOWA DETONATION OF DEGRADED BOMB MATERIALS: ‘A CONSENSUS DECISION’

While the air monitoring results have been encouraging, Zeldin emphasized that the agency is continuing its environmental assessment, comparing thousands of samples collected before and after the detonation.

"We are going to make sure we do all of our due diligence," he said.

The EPA administrator said the agency expects to begin releasing the first post-detonation sampling results as early as Friday night.

"Hopefully that confirms what we saw at the air monitor," he said.

The agency's ongoing assessment comes after Wednesday's controlled detonation of the bomb-making chemical in Middletown, Iowa.

DR MARC SIEGEL: IOWA'S CANCER RATE IS RISING; ONE ANSWER MAY BE FOUND IN THE WATER

Roughly 5 tons of degraded lead azide were destroyed after being deemed unsafe and unstable amid concerns that a plume of potentially toxic dust could drift toward Missouri in the wake of the blast.

The EPA has collected more than 3,000 air, water, soil and dust samples, including 1,639 before the detonation to establish a baseline and 1,618 afterward to assess potential environmental changes.

In a separate update Friday, the EPA reported that it had completed 88% of post-detonation sampling at homes where samples had also been collected before the blast and was working to complete the remaining assessments.

The agency said air monitoring concluded Thursday afternoon after 30 consecutive hours of no detectable airborne lead.

EPA REPORTS 'ZERO DETECTION OF AIRBORNE LEAD' DAY AFTER IOWA LEAD AZIDE DETONATION

President Donald Trump also sought to reassure residents Thursday about their safety following the detonation.

"They're 100% safe," he told reporters.

He emphasized that the U.S. Army did a "phenomenal job" with the detonation.

Fox News Digital's Greg Norman-Diamond contributed to this report.

item.title: Multiple Florida State captains refuse handshakes with Florida at coin toss, raising sportsmanship questions
item.description: Florida State Seminoles captains refused handshakes at the coin toss vs the Florida Gators, drawing fan backlash, with only Duce Robinson offering a hand.
item.content:encoded:
The day after Thanksgiving kicks off the main slate of rivalry week in college football.

Thanksgiving ushered in several days of rivalry matchups, with teams across the country facing their top foes, often in-state rivals.

Before Florida and Florida State kicked off in the state's capital city, the rivalry’s intensity was on display in the lead-up to the pregame coin toss. FSU's team captains appeared to decline the customary handshake. Multiple players were seen with their hands behind their backs or at their sides.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Duce Robinson, a Florida State wide receiver who was on crutches, appeared to be the only one of the four Seminoles captains to reach out for handshake at midfield. The exchange sparked fan reactions on social media.

"Duce is only class act there. The rest have to go, especially the twins," an FSU fan replied to a video showing the interaction on X.

"We aren’t in a position to be acting hard and refusing to dap people up. Bad look," another Noles fan wrote on X.

IT TURNS OUT FLORIDA GATORS COACH JON SUMRALL IS JUST AS SUPERSTITIOUS AS HIS FANBASE

Once the game kicked off, Florida running back Jadan Baugh's 3-yard touchdown helped lift the No. 20 Gators to a 26-10 win over FSU. Baugh became the first player in program history to record consecutive 1,000-yard rushing seasons.

Baugh finished the day with 77 yards for Florida, who have won six of eight games against FSU.

Gators quarterback Aaron Philo threw for 127 yards for Florida before leaving because of an injury. Backup Trammel Jones Jr. had a 1-yard touchdown run but also had a fourth-quarter interception. The Seminoles, down to their fifth running back due to injury, managed just 98 total rushing yards.

Florida is bowl eligible but will not know its postseason destination until Dec. 6. Florida State’s season is over, and the program will await the arrival of its next head coach, Glenn Schumann, who is not expected to take over full-time in Tallahassee until after No. 1 Georgia’s likely College Football Playoff run ends.

Schumann is Georgia’s defensive coordinator.

Georgia will face in-state rival Georgia Tech on Saturday. The Bulldogs have already clinched a spot in what is expected to be the final SEC Championship game. Alabama, Texas and Tennessee are all vying for the second spot in the conference championship game in Atlanta.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Seahawks, 49ers matchup changes drastically as Brock Purdy ruled out while Sam Darnold returns from injury
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks will start Sam Darnold as he is back from injury, while the San Francisco 49ers will be without Brock Purdy ahead of a pivotal matchup with an ankle injury.
item.content:encoded:
The Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers are heading into their pivotal matchup on Sunday in very different places.

The Seahawks will start Sam Darnold, who missed the previous two games with quad and rib injuries, while the 49ers will be without star quarterback Brock Purdy due to an ankle injury he suffered last week. Backup quarterback Mac Jones will start in Purdy's stead.

Drew Lock has held down the fort while Darnold has missed time with multiple injuries this season, as the 30-year-old quarterback has a 3-0 record, but that record might as well be 4-0. In Week 1, Darnold went down early in the first quarter and Lock played the majority of the game, helping lead the Seahawks to a win over the New England Patriots.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

While the Seahawks are happy to get Darnold back, they hope he will revert to his 2025 form down the stretch, as he has dealt with turnover issues this season. In seven games this season, Darnold has a 60.2% completion percentage with 1,478 yards, 10 touchdowns and nine interceptions. The Seahawks have a 3-4 record in Darnold's starts this season.

All of the numbers reflect a dip compared to 2025. In 17 games last season, the Seahawks went 14-3 as Darnold completed 67.7% of his passes for 4,048 yards, 25 touchdowns and 14 interceptions.

The Seahawks are 6-4 this season and at risk of missing the playoffs despite winning the Super Bowl last year because the NFC West — and the NFC in general — is stacked with contenders. A win over their division rival would go a long way toward helping them reach the postseason for the second straight year.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Their path to victory is a lot easier without Purdy, whose play has him in the MVP conversation this year. Despite the 49ers' wide receiver room being ravaged by injury, the 26-year-old quarterback has thrived. In 10 games, Purdy has completed 71% of his passes for 2,624 yards, 23 touchdowns and five interceptions while running for 222 yards and two touchdowns.

The former Iowa State star's play is a massive reason why the 49ers are 9-1 and have the best record in the NFC.

Jones played in 11 games last season, starting eight of them, for an injured Purdy, and was productive. He had a 5-3 record in his starts and completed 69. 6% of his passes for 2,151 yards with 13 touchdowns and six interceptions.

Because he played so well, teams inquired about acquiring the 28-year-old in the offseason and at the trade deadline, but the 49ers rebuffed all offers. The Pro Bowler has appeared in three games this season but hasn't played any meaningful snaps as he only entered games in garbage time.

Jones and the 49ers will try to secure their stranglehold on the division and conference when they play the Seahawks on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET.

item.title: Taliban reportedly strips women of their names in Afghan province, now being called 'goat' or 'grandmother'
item.description: The Taliban reportedly banned women's names from official records in an Afghan province, five years after reclaiming power amid Biden's chaotic withdrawal.
item.content:encoded:
The Taliban have reportedly banned the use of women's names in official documents in a northern Afghan province, with some women being referred to by degrading animal names, according to a report by Spanish newspaper El País.

The latest assault on women's rights under Taliban rule reportedly extends to medical records and prescriptions in Afghanistan's Balkh province, raising fears that the restrictions could spread nationwide.

Healthcare workers and other public employees have been instructed to address women as "Bibi," meaning grandmother or old woman, according to reporting by Afghan news outlet Zan Times and The Guardian cited by El País.

MOSCOW, TALIBAN FORGE MILITARY ALLIANCE IN POWER GRAB AFTER US AFGHANISTAN EXIT: REPORTS

Afghan women's rights activist Lalah Osmany, who is based in Germany, told El País that testimony from women, doctors and civil rights activists indicates some women are also being referred to in degrading terms such as "goat" or "cow."

"This is a systematic process of dehumanization," Osmany told the newspaper.

An Afghan activist speaking under a pseudonym confirmed the reported order to El País, although she said it had so far been ignored.

Zubaida Akbar, who directs the Afghanistan program at women's rights organization Femena, warned that the Taliban could eventually impose the ban nationwide, citing previous instances in which local restrictions were expanded across the country.

IRAN FLOGS FEMALE SINGER 74 TIMES FOR PERFORMING WITHOUT HIJAB IN VIRAL YOUTUBE CONCERT

Femena has counted more than 144 decrees restricting Afghan women's rights, according to El País.

Girls have been barred from studying beyond age 12, while women have been shut out of most professions and subjected to restrictions on speaking in public, the newspaper reported.

Some Afghan women have resorted to running underground businesses and secret schools in defiance of Taliban restrictions, according to Associated Press reporting published Nov. 17.

IRAN TO EXECUTE FIRST FEMALE PROTESTER TIED TO ANTI-REGIME UNREST

One Kabul beauty salon owner, whose identity was concealed for her safety, reopened her business after authorities raided her previous salon and confiscated her equipment.

"But now, they won’t even allow that; for women in Afghanistan, working has become a crime," she told the AP.

An assistant teacher at a secret school in Kabul described living in constant fear of arrest.

"We are absolutely terrified of that possibility," she told the AP.

Mohammad Aslam, a spokesman for the Taliban's Ministry for the Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice, defended the broader restrictions in comments to the AP, saying women could conduct business and social affairs provided they adhered to Islamic Sharia law and existing laws.

Osmany also warned that the reported naming ban could endanger female patients by increasing the risk of medical errors if prescriptions and medical records are filed under identical names.

Afghan women already face severe barriers to medical care under Taliban rule, including restrictions on male doctors treating female patients and bans on women pursuing medical training, according to El País.

In 2017, Osmany launched a campaign to have Afghan women's names included on official documents, including their children's birth certificates.

ARMY VET LAWMAKER MARKS ABBEY GATE ANNIVERSARY WITH BLISTERING MESSAGE FOR BIDEN-HARRIS: 'ABJECT FAILURE'

Despite receiving death threats from extremists, her campaign helped secure a change in 2020 allowing mothers' names to be voluntarily included on such documents. That progress was short-lived.

The Taliban swept back into power in August 2021 as the U.S.-backed Afghan government collapsed amid then-President Joe Biden's chaotic military withdrawal, leaving the country once again under the control of Islamist extremists.

The withdrawal drew widespread condemnation after 13 American service members, mostly Marines, were killed in an ISIS-K terrorist attack during the evacuation from Kabul.

Biden faced further backlash from Gold Star families after checking his watch during the dignified transfer of fallen American troops at Dover Air Force Base in Delaware.

Five years later, Afghan women and girls have seen hard-won freedoms stripped away under Taliban rule. Now, activists warn, even their very identities are under threat.

"Calling a woman by her real name in Afghanistan is an act of resistance," Osmany told El País.

item.title: American Airlines planes clip wings during busy holiday travel weekend at Reagan National in DC
item.description: The FAA will investigate after two American Airlines Boeing 737s clipped wings at Reagan National Airport in Washington, D.C., sending both back to gates.
item.content:encoded:
Federal authorities are investigating after two American Airlines Boeing 737-800s clipped wings as they taxied for takeoff Friday at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA) in Washington, D.C., forcing both aircraft to return to their gates.

The Federal Aviation Administration told Fox News Digital American Airlines Flight 638, bound for Dallas, clipped the wing of American Airlines Flight 2152, headed to Chicago, while waiting in the departure queue at about 5:10 p.m.

Both planes returned to their gates and were checked by Airports Authority Fire and Rescue personnel, according to the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority.

UPS CARGO PLANE, COPA AIRLINES PASSENGER JET COLLIDE AT MIAMI AIRPORT, LEAVING 2 INJURED

American Airlines told Fox News Digital there were no injuries, and both aircraft have been removed from service for inspection by its maintenance team.

"We apologize to our customers for the inconvenience and are working to get them on their way as soon as possible," American Airlines wrote in a statement.

REAGAN NATIONAL AIRPORT MAKES DRASTIC CHANGE FOLLOWING DEADLY 2025 MIDAIR COLLISION

The MWAA said no other flights were disrupted during the busy holiday weekend, and the airline noted customers from both flights will re-depart Friday evening.

The FAA will investigate the incident.

A similar incident occurred at DCA in April 2025, when another plane bumped the wing of an aircraft carrying several U.S. lawmakers and two former Gaza hostages as it waited to take off.

Rep. Nick LaLota, R-N.Y., told Fox News Digital at the time that he was on the plane alongside Reps. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J., Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., Richie Torres, D-N.Y., and Adriano Espaillat, D-N.Y. No injuries were reported.

"Serving in Congress has come with some once in a lifetime experiences… like just now while stationary on the runway at DCA, another plane just bumped into our wing," LaLota wrote in a social media post shortly after the collision.

Both planes involved in the April 2025 collision were operated by American Airlines, Fox News Digital previously reported.

"Congressman LaLota intends to bring this firsthand experience to his work in Congress, advocating for stronger aviation oversight and enhanced public safety to help prevent similar incidents in the future," LaLota's office told Fox News Digital at the time.

item.title: It turns out Florida Gators coach Jon Sumrall is just as superstitious as his fanbase
item.description: Jon Sumrall made a last-minute switch away from the Florida Gators' blue helmets before the rivalry game with Florida State, and the gambit paid off.
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Gators and Florida State Seminoles played in a rare Friday afternoon game in the latest chapter of their storied rivalry.

Although there were no stakes on the line as far as the College Football Playoff is concerned, these two teams hate each other to the point that the fear of losing is enough to get the juices flowing.

Florida head coach Jon Sumrall was a newbie to this rivalry, but he certainly understood what a win (or a loss) in Tallahassee would do for him in year one.

THESE ONCE-ANNUAL COLLEGE RIVALRIES USED TO DEFINE COLLEGE FOOTBALL AND NEED TO MAKE A COMEBACK ASAP

You don't even need to hear him talk about it to know how much this game meant to him, as his actions spoke much louder than his words this week.

All year, the Florida Gators were scheduled to wear blue helmets in their regular season finale against FSU.

JON SUMRALL SAYS TEENAGE SON SENT HIM RUTHLESS TEXT BEFORE LEAVING FLORIDA'S LOSS TO SOUTH CAROLINA EARLY

The blue helmets were nearly omnipresent in all of their promotional material leading up to the game, but there's just one problem.

The Gators are 1-2 this season while wearing their blue lids, with the lone win coming against FCS program Campbell.

Sumrall very likely knew about this, and being the superstitious psycho that he is, the Florida head honcho decided to call an audible.

I'm sure all Gator fans can find comfort in knowing that their head football coach is literally the same as they are: a complete lunatic.

URBAN MEYER JOINS DAN DAKICH, GUSHES ABOUT NEW FLORIDA HEAD COACH JON SUMRALL: 'I LOVE THAT GUY'

We know head coaches are creatures of habit, but this takes things to a whole new level.

Having watched Sumrall operate both professionally and as a fan, I can guarantee you he was acutely aware that his team stinks wearing blue helmets.

Is there a strategic advantage to the switch? Absolutely not.

But it's great to see the man trying anything he can to get an extra win this season.

And his efforts were rewarded, as the Gators took down their arch rival FSU by a score of 26-10.

So, maybe Sumrall was on to something after all.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers claims he was barred from Steelers facility before infamous interview in message to Al Michaels
item.description: Al Michaels said Aaron Rodgers told him Mike McCarthy never called and that he was barred from the Pittsburgh Steelers facility, prompting his rant on "The Pat McAfee Show."
item.content:encoded:
The Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy saga has a new chapter.

During the Pittsburgh Steelers' dominating 27-5 win over the Denver Broncos on Friday at Acrisure Stadium, Amazon Prime Video broadcaster Al Michaels said he heard from Rodgers earlier in the day.

The 82-year-old reported that the four-time MVP was barred from the Steelers' facility after being made inactive on Tuesday. Michaels said Rodgers told him that he never heard from McCarthy, and that the Steelers leaked the news he was being made inactive at 11:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday and barred him from the facility, which is why he decided to go on ESPN's "The Pat McAfee Show."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

It is unclear at what point the Steelers barred him from the facility, but Rodgers did not show up to the building on Wednesday before going scorched-earth on Pat McAfee's show in the afternoon. He was released from the team shortly after the interview.

It also appears that the 42-year-old quarterback had heard some of the criticism that has been lobbed his way about protecting the integrity of the locker room. Michaels said that Rodgers told him the code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership.

AARON RODGERS NOT RETURNING TO STEELERS, SAYS MIKE MCCARTHY FALLS ASLEEP IN MEETINGS AND IS 'UNWELL'

The Steelers, despite finding themselves in headlines and on talk shows for reasons other than their upcoming game, played a great football game on Friday. Steelers ownership backed McCarthy after Rodgers' comments, and his team rewarded ownership for the support.

The Steelers defense scored two touchdowns, and quarterback Mason Rudolph played a mistake-free game to lead Pittsburgh to a much-needed win.

Amid all the drama this week, with the Steelers entering Friday's game at 6-4 and on the edge of the AFC playoff picture, it almost seemed like a footnote that they had to defeat the Broncos to remain in contention for the AFC North and Wild Card picture.

Now at 7-4, they have given themselves an opportunity to chase the Bengals down and win the AFC North. They will just be doing it without Rodgers.

item.title: Steelers silence the Aaron Rodgers noise, cruise past Broncos to remain perfect at home on Black Friday
item.description: T.J. Watt and Jalen Ramsey turned Bo Nix mistakes into touchdowns as the Pittsburgh Steelers snapped Denver's six-game winning streak in the rain.
item.content:encoded:
The Pittsburgh Steelers were placed firmly under the microscope this week. Aaron Rodgers’ benching, revealing interview and subsequent departure sent shockwaves through the NFL.

Amid the shakeup, coach Mike McCarthy and the Steelers turned their attention to a high-stakes Black Friday matchup with the Denver Broncos. Pittsburgh entered Friday on a two-game losing streak, while Denver had won six straight.

But the Steelers embraced the underdog role Friday, upsetting the AFC West-leading Broncos 27-5. Mason Rudolph started at quarterback and threw a touchdown pass, while Pittsburgh’s other stars delivered key plays. T.J. Watt recovered a Bo Nix fumble in the end zone for a touchdown, and Jalen Ramsey intercepted Nix and returned it for another score.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

D.K. Metcalf appeared to show his support for Rodgers after hauling in what was arguably his best catch since joining the Steelers in the first quarter. item.title: Mamdani handed out $95K in staff raises the same day he warned of $12B budget deficit: report
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani approved $850,000 in raises for City Hall aides in his first year, according to payroll records reviewed by the New York Post.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani approved roughly $850,000 in pay raises for dozens of City Hall aides during his first year in office, according to municipal payroll records reviewed by the New York Post.

The records show the raises were distributed to at least 46 staffers since Mamdani took office in January, bringing total compensation increases near $1 million.

The Post counted 21 new hires who received raises totaling $450,000 before their first anniversary on the job, more than twice the combined number of first-year employees who got raises under Eric Adams and Bill de Blasio.

MAMDANI TURNS ON NEW YORK CITY TEACHERS UNION WITH LAWSUIT BLOCKING PAY RAISES FOR EDUCATORS

On Jan. 28, five City Hall employees were granted salary increases totaling $95,000 on the same day Mamdani announced New York City faced an estimated $12 billion budget deficit, the records show. The mayor’s office later lowered that projected deficit to approximately $5.4 billion.

The mayor’s office on Nov. 12 confirmed the city’s fiscal 2027 budget rose $3.3 billion from the budget adopted in June, reaching $129.2 billion.

MAMDANI'S TAXPAYER-FUNDED INFLUENCER ARMY ACCUSED OF PLOTTING PRESSURE CAMPAIGN AGAINST NYC CEOS

The payroll disclosures detail significant salary adjustments across several executive staff positions.

Julia Simcoe and Jacob Russell each received raises of more than $60,000, bringing their salaries to $148,000 and $145,000, respectively, the Post reported. Three other City Hall staffers received raises ranging from $30,000 to $45,000.

MAMDANI’S AFFORDABILITY REVOLUTION STUMBLED AS RENT COSTS SOAR TO RECORD HIGHS

The salary increases come as Mamdani, who took office Jan. 1 as the city's first self-described socialist mayor, faces fiscal constraints and administrative hurdles on core campaign pledges.

Mamdani’s plan to eliminate bus fares across the five boroughs has stalled after pushback from New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, who noted the Metropolitan Transportation Authority cannot absorb the loss of revenue from fare boxes. While Mamdani’s campaign estimated the initiative would cost $700 million, the New York City Independent Budget Office (IBO) projected that fully eliminating fares would cost New York State roughly $1.1 billion.

EXPERTS SCORCH MAMDANI'S GROCERY PLAN AS AN 'ILLUSION' THAT WILL HAVE TAXPAYERS FOOTING THE BILL

The administration has also faced capacity limits with its universal childcare initiative. A pilot program aimed at 2-year-olds launched with 2,000 available seats but drew more than 5,700 applicants, leaving roughly 3,700 children on waitlists. The program cost $73 million to launch, and the IBO estimated an expanded citywide version would cost $425 million by 2028.

Meanwhile, Mamdani's plan to establish five city-run grocery stores that sell items 30% below market value has drawn skepticism from retail analysts and economists who question whether the discounts can be sustained without ongoing taxpayer subsidies.

Fox News Digital asked the mayor's office what civil service guidelines justified the early salary bumps, why raises were authorized the same day Mamdani warned of a $12 billion deficit and how City Hall reconciles the payroll increases with budget constraints on programs like universal childcare and free transit.

A spokesperson for City Hall did not immediately return a request for comment.

Fox News Digital’s Leo Briceno contributed to this report.

item.title: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum protests new DEA tip line for reporting criminals, corrupt officials
item.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said Mexico filed a formal complaint over the DEA tip line that lets anonymous callers report cartel operatives.
item.content:encoded:
Mexico has filed a formal complaint with the United States over a new Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) tip line that allows anonymous callers to report corrupt government officials and cartel operatives, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said Friday.

Sheinbaum, who has repeatedly pushed back against U. S. actions targeting Mexican drug cartels, announced the diplomatic protest during her daily morning briefing.

"We have made it very clear in our relationship with the United States that the relationship is one of coordination, not subordination," she said.

DRUG CARTEL KINGPIN AMONG TARGETS IN SWEEPING TRUMP CRACKDOWN ON ALLEGED MEXICAN CORRUPTION NETWORK

The Trump administration has argued that Mexico has not done enough to combat cartels or stem the flow of fentanyl into the United States, while Sheinbaum has accused Washington of infringing on Mexican sovereignty.

"The DEA has plenty of work to do in its own country. A lot," Sheinbaum said Thursday. "The first thing it should do is investigate corruption in the United States linked to organized crime, or what they call terrorist groups."

COAST GUARD FIREFIGHT PUTS US, MEXICO AT ODDS DESPITE COORDINATED BORDER OPERATIONS

On Wednesday, DEA Administrator Terry Cole announced the launch of the tip line, saying anonymous callers could report members and associates of designated terrorist organizations, corrupt officials who benefit from them, criminal networks and money launderers financing narco-terrorism in the Mexican state of Sinaloa, home to the Sinaloa Cartel, one of the country's most powerful and violent drug trafficking groups.

Cole added that phone numbers for a similar tip line targeting the state of Jalisco would be released later.

DOJ FLOODED WITH THOUSANDS OF FRAUD TIPS AFTER CASH INCENTIVE LAUNCH, TRUMP OFFICIAL SAYS

Sheinbaum urged Washington to focus on curbing drug use and cartel activity within its own borders, adding that Mexico would continue to confront criminal organizations to prevent drugs from reaching the United States.

"The United States has a responsibility to its people to address drug use, as well as to arrest members of the drug cartels operating in the United States," Sheinbaum said. "We cannot have this view that the responsibility lies with Mexico."

EXCLUSIVE: FENTANYL DEATHS PLUNGE 22% AS TRUMP WHITE HOUSE TOUTS CRACKDOWN ON DEADLY DRUG CRISIS

Her remarks came days after Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro," an ally of a Sinaloa Cartel faction, was captured in Mexico during a joint U.S.-Mexican operation. The State Department had previously offered a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest.

item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays will reportedly be hearing some sweet tunes next season.

In his first 46 games with the Yankees in 2024, he played third base and hit .273 with 11 home runs, 23 RBIs and 18 stolen bases. item.title: Low levels of common vitamin could be stealing nearly 30 minutes of your sleep
item.description: Low vitamin D blood levels were linked to about 23 minutes less sleep per night in a new study of adults 40 and older that used wearable sensors.
item.content:encoded:
Middle-aged and older adults with low levels of vitamin D slept about 23 minutes less per night than people with normal levels, according to a new study that tracked sleep with wearable sensors.

The study, led by the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health and the National Institute on Aging, used data collected from 2012 to 2019 as part of the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging.

The researchers looked at blood tests and sleep data from 460 adults ages 40 and older, averaging 71 years of age.

ONE TYPE OF SLEEP LINKED TO DRAMATICALLY LOWER RISK OF DEMENTIA, PARKINSON'S AND 81 OTHER DISEASES

After dividing the participants into three groups by vitamin D level, they found that the highest group slept nearly 20 minutes longer each night than the group with the lowest levels.

People with lower levels also stayed awake longer after waking up at night — a pattern that held regardless of age, gender or race.

The connection between vitamin D and sleep was strongest among Black participants, who made up about 22% of the group.

"Black adults in the United States have a higher prevalence of vitamin D deficiency and sleep disturbances compared to White adults, and may benefit more from increasing vitamin D levels," lead author Diefei Chen, a doctoral candidate in epidemiology at the Bloomberg School, said in a press release.

CAN WEARABLES DETECT HEART PROBLEMS EARLY? DOCTOR BREAKS DOWN REAL DATA

Most earlier studies on vitamin D and sleep relied on people reporting how well they thought they slept. In this study, researchers used blood draws and actigraphs, which are watch-like motion sensors that measure sleep and wake times.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The team also checked vitamin B12, which previous studies linked to sleep. While higher levels correlated with less nighttime wakefulness in women and more in men, the authors noted the results were statistically inconclusive.

The findings were published on Oct. 14 in The Journal of Gerontology: Medical Sciences.

Poor sleep and vitamin D deficiency are both widespread among older adults, with previous research linking sleep disturbances to higher risks of dementia, heart disease and diabetes.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The study had several limitations. Because the researchers looked at snapshots of data rather than testing a treatment in a clinical trial, they could only establish a link between vitamin D and sleep.

The findings did not prove that low levels cause poor sleep or that taking supplements will fix it.

Because blood tests can't distinguish between vitamin D from sunlight, food or supplements, the study could not determine whether the source matters.

In addition, the researchers did not track whether changing a person's vitamin D levels over several years leads to changes in their sleep.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Because everyone in the study was 40 or older and had no cognitive impairment, the results may not apply to younger people or adults with memory and thinking problems.

"These findings suggest that we should investigate more thoroughly whether boosting vitamin D levels can improve sleep health," senior author Adam Spira, a mental health professor at the Bloomberg School, said in the news release.

item.title: Eagles kicker didn't get ex-NFLer's memo about not digging into post-game Thanksgiving food
item.description: Derek Carr shares the cold Thanksgiving turkey warning that Eagles hero Jake Elliott apparently missed after his 59-yard field goal beat the Cowboys.
item.content:encoded:
Thanksgiving is a day for cramming absurd amounts of food into your mouth hole — and giving thanks, I suppose — but one ex-NFLer has a pro tip about when to show a little restraint.

And it would seem that Eagles' Thanksgiving hero Jake Elliott missed the memo.

Back in 2021, Derek Carr also led his team — the Las Vegas Raiders at the time — to a Thanksgiving win over the Dallas Cowboys.

COWBOYS LEGEND RANDY WHITE REVEALS INTENSE ENCOUNTER BETWEEN HIS MOTHER AND EAGLES FANS DURING PLAYING CAREER

As is tradition, he got to help himself to some of the broadcast's Turkey Day grub along with that game's hero, kicker Daniel Carlson.

"I have to share this every year," Carr said on his podcast "Home Grown with David & Derek Carr," per Daily Mail.

"So we're up there, we do the interview... and obviously Daniel made his kick. We're like: 'Daniel, you're going to eat the turkey.'"

Of course, few things top a good Thanksgiving meal, but we usually mean one that came straight out of the oven.

"It's definitely cold... [but] he goes to take a bite, and he says: 'Oh, delicious!'" Carr recalled. "And right as we walk away, I said, 'How was it?' He said: 'It was the grossest thing I've ever tasted.'"

It makes sense, especially for a game that goes down to the wire, that the food was prepped well in advance.

Of course, that also means it's not in its optimal eating window.

GIANTS STAR CAM SKATTEBO REVEALS THE ODD PREGAME MEAL THAT CAUSED TO HIM TO PUKE MID-GAME

Well, Elliott must not be subscribed to Carr's podcast because after sealing the Eagles' historic 39-38 comeback win with a 59-yard field goal, he dug right in.

Hey, the taste of sweet, sweet victory goes nicely with food that was probably intended just to be set dressing.

But, lest you think that Elliott had to do his Black Friday shopping while lying on the floor of his bathroom between bouts with food poisoning, think again.

The Eagles' hero was right back at it, getting fans fired up before the Philadelphia Flyers' Black Friday game against the Vancouver Canucks.

Looks like he fared better than most of us did on Thanksgiving, even though our food was much fresher than some stuffing warmed by studio lights.

item.title: NBC pulls controversial anti-Israel ad after igniting fury from Jewish groups
item.description: NBC pulled a controversial anti-Israel ad that aired during a primetime "Saturday Night Live" Thanksgiving special, sparking backlash among Jewish groups.
item.content:encoded:
NBC has pulled a controversial anti-Israel ad from its airwaves after sparking backlash over the Thanksgiving holiday, Fox News Digital has confirmed.

During a Thanksgiving-themed "Saturday Night Live" primetime special Wednesday night, NBC aired an ad featuring a girl raising money for a $400 bike, juxtaposing her with a Palestinian girl with a missing leg standing on crutches in front of a pile of rubble.

"Every three seconds, our government sends $400 of taxpayer money to Israel to do this," a narrator tells viewers while showing the injured Gazan child on screen.

MS RACHEL CALLS SILENCE ON GAZA CONFLICT 'F---ED UP,' SAYS IT UPSETS HER SO MUCH SHE NOW SWEARS

The 30-second ad, funded by the IMEU (Institute for Middle East Understanding) Policy Project, directs viewers to a website named No More For Israel, criticizing what it describes as the U.S. government's weapons "giveaway" to Israel and accusing the Jewish state of "committing a genocide" against Palestinians. The site urges Americans to pressure lawmakers to oppose any weapons deal with Israel.

Jewish groups and pro-Israel advocates criticized the ad as antisemitic, with many pointing out that the ad makes no mention that the ongoing conflict in Gaza began with the Oct. 7 terrorist attack committed by Hamas against Israel.

MANDANI GRILLED ON RHETORIC TOWARD OCT 7, COMBATTING ANTISEMITISM AS JEWISH NEW YORKERS FEAR CURRENT CLIMATE

"NBC took money to tell millions of Americans that our support for Israel is responsible for the horrific injury of a Palestinian child," American Jewish Committee CEO Ted Deutch wrote on X. 

"Here’s what the ad leaves out: the vicious Hamas terrorists who launched this war on October 7 by slaughtering, raping, and kidnapping Israelis, dragging hostages into Gaza, and then fighting from among Palestinian civilians, with horrific consequences for Israelis and Gazans alike.

"The suffering of Palestinian civilians is real and heartbreaking. But using that suffering to demonize Israel while writing Hamas out of the story isn’t an honest debate," the former Democratic congressman continued. 

"We can debate American policy and assistance to Israel. And yes, this was a paid advertisement. But 'we were paid to run it' cannot be the end of the discussion. Networks decide what they will and will not put on the air every day. NBC chose to take the money and run this ad.

"It should explain why and how an ad this one-sided and manipulative met its standards for what it will put on the air. And if this meets NBC’s standards, Americans deserve to know what those standards are."

The Israeli-American Council (IAC) characterized the ad as a clear example of "antisemitic blood libel aimed at denying the Jewish state its right to defend itself against terrorists and murderers."

"Words and images have consequences," the group shared in a statement to Fox News Digital. "They can normalize antisemitic hatred, embolden people to act on it and endanger innocent lives." 

The IAC called on NBC to "come clean about how this advertisement met its own standards and ensure it is not aired again." 

Anti-Defamation League CEO Jonathan Greenblatt also slammed NBC's decision to air the ad.

"Broadcasting an ad that blatantly demonizes the Jewish state and makes false claims about the use of American taxpayer dollars during primetime on the eve of a family holiday isn’t just insensitive. It’s indefensible," he wrote. 

"At a moment of escalating antisemitism, there is no rationale to justify fanning the flames with such a twisted narrative."

UK ANTISEMITISM ADVISOR LAUNCHES PROBE INTO BBC, SAYS CULTURE DEMANDS JEWISH STAFFERS 'JUSTIFY' EXISTENCE

"Modern day Nazi propaganda compliments of NBC. Every person who approved this ad buy should be identified and terminated," the advocacy group Stop Antisemitism wrote.

A source familiar with the matter told Fox News Digital that senior leadership at NBC was unaware of the ad until after it aired and that the network intends to reevaluate its ad review process going forward. The Wall Street Journal's Joe Flint first reported NBC's decision.

A spokesperson for NBC declined to comment.

item.title: Eagles running back compares heated argument with coach on sideline to arguing politics at Thanksgiving
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley likened his sideline argument with head coach Nick Sirianni to arguing politics at Thanksgiving.
item.content:encoded:
In case you were wondering what arguments are like on an NFL sideline, Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley peeled back the curtain for you: It's like arguing politics at Thanksgiving.

After the Eagles were stopped by the Dallas Cowboys in the first half of their thrilling 39-38 win on Thursday at AT&T Stadium, Shipley and head coach Nick Sirianni got into an argument on the sideline.

"Emotions were running high," Shipley told reporters after the game. "Like on Thanksgiving, all families are arguing about politics and the drunk uncle."

"I've got so much love for Coach Nick and him as the leader of this football team."

Shipley said the two talked about it later when cooler heads prevailed and said there is no hard feelings between him and his head coach. The 24-year-old running back said Sirianni's passionate coaching style resonates with him.

"I mean, it really resonates with me because I wear my emotions on my sleeve as well. I have throughout my whole career and so for me to be able to just see him lead us in that way. It really resonates with me and I think resonates with everybody in this locker room," Shipley said.

Eagles star left tackle Jordan Mailata confirmed that Shipley and Sirianni were on good terms.

item.title: From turkey shortages to helicopter deliveries: The extraordinary history of Thanksgiving during war
item.description: The U.S. military has delivered Thanksgiving dinner to troops from Civil War Union troops to Vietnam's War Zone D, a tradition born in wartime.
item.content:encoded:
In November 1966, 12 American soldiers stationed at an isolated outpost in a Vietnamese war zone were about as far from a traditional Thanksgiving at home as they could get.

Their only means of resupply was by air. But the U.S. military was determined to get them Thanksgiving dinner anyway.

A mess sergeant at Bien Hoa prepared turkey and all the trimmings, packed the meal into insulated containers and sent it by helicopter into War Zone D, where three officers and nine enlisted men of a 5th Special Forces detachment sat down to Thanksgiving dinner, according to Defense Department records preserved by the National Archives.

The delivery was one piece of a massive logistical effort the U.S. military has undertaken during wars spanning generations to get traditional Thanksgiving meals to troops serving in combat zones.

From civilians sending tens of thousands of turkeys to Union troops during the Civil War to helicopters carrying hot meals to soldiers in Korea, the holiday has been observed through some of the nation's most consequential conflicts.

Thanksgiving became a national tradition in the midst of war. President Abraham Lincoln issued his 1863 Thanksgiving proclamation as the Civil War entered its third year, calling on Americans to observe the final Thursday of November as a day of "Thanksgiving and Praise."

By the following year, Americans on the home front were mounting a massive effort to get Thanksgiving dinner to Union troops.

Former War Department official Charles A. Dana later recalled the "great turkey movement" of November 1864. In New York alone, organizers reported having 20,000 turkeys ready to send to the front, according to Dana's account. A Philadelphia committee sought transportation for another 4,000 destined for troops serving under Gen. Philip Sheridan.

By World War II, the effort to put turkey on troops' Thanksgiving tables had grown so large that it affected whether Americans at home could find one for their own.

In August 1943, the War Food Administration restricted most civilian turkey sales as the government sought millions of pounds for the armed forces. An initial goal of at least 10 million pounds for troops overseas was expanded to include military installations at home, and the government ultimately obtained roughly 30 million pounds before the order was lifted in October, according to wartime government records.

A year later, delivering Thanksgiving dinner near the front could carry its own risks.

102-YEAR-OLD NAVY VETERAN STILL CRAVES HOT WINGS AFTER 102 COMBAT MISSIONS IN KOREA: 'I MIGHT MAKE IT TO 115'

In Germany's Hürtgen Forest, Lt. Paul Boesch of the 121st Infantry Regiment later recalled being told that hot turkey dinners had arrived for his men amid some of the European campaign's most grueling fighting. Boesch protested that sending soldiers to collect the food would expose them to German artillery, but the order to distribute the meal stood.

His fears proved well-founded. As troops gathered to retrieve the food, German artillery struck the area, killing and wounding several men, according to Boesch's account.

Six years later, American troops were again eating Thanksgiving dinner near the front, this time in the bitter cold of North Korea.

On Thanksgiving Day 1950, Marines around the Chosin Reservoir were served turkey and cranberry sauce, candied sweet potatoes, fruitcake and mince pie. In the subzero temperatures, the food quickly began to freeze.

US NAVY RELEASES PHOTOS OF 'FRESH MEALS,' PUSHES BACK ON REPORTS OF FOOD SHORTAGES ON MIDDLE EAST WARSHIPS

The dinner came as U.S. commanders remained optimistic that the war could soon be over. The following day, Gen. Douglas MacArthur launched an offensive that became known as the "Home-by-Christmas" campaign.

Instead, Chinese forces entered the fighting in massive numbers. Within days of Thanksgiving, Marines around Chosin were surrounded and battling through one of the most brutal engagements of the Korean War.

More than half a century later, another generation of American troops was spending Thanksgiving at war in Iraq and Afghanistan.

In 2003, President George W. Bush secretly flew into Baghdad to surprise roughly 600 troops gathered for Thanksgiving dinner at Baghdad International Airport. Air Force One approached with its cabin shades drawn and lights dimmed amid tight security surrounding the trip.

"I was just looking for a warm meal somewhere," Bush joked before addressing the troops and helping serve Thanksgiving dinner.

In Afghanistan, getting that dinner to troops stationed far from major bases could require a different kind of operation.

On Thanksgiving 2007, helicopters carried turkeys and traditional fixings from Bagram Airfield to soldiers at remote firebases in the Tagab Valley, according to a contemporaneous U.S. military account.

It was the first hot meal some of the soldiers had eaten in months. Because the positions still had to be defended, troops rotated between Thanksgiving dinner and standing watch.

"The white meat was magnificent," Pfc. Matt Lorimer of the 82nd Airborne Division said.

At another remote Afghan outpost two years later, troops spent a month fattening five scrawny turkeys purchased locally for Thanksgiving. But five birds were not enough to feed roughly 150 soldiers.

Additional turkey was flown from the United States to Bagram Airfield and then transported to the outpost. Even that was not the end of the journey.

A handful of soldiers were manning an observation post on a mountain spur roughly 6,900 feet above sea level. Their Thanksgiving dinner was packed up and flown by helicopter up the mountain to them.
